thread:
mika: heads up — Acme ran a security review on their Private/VPC deployment and flagged two things: (1) unexpected outbound flows to third-party monitoring during normal inference, (2) requests for proof of KMS/HSM audit events + retention policy. They want a write-up + remediation steps by EOD. cc @jonas @sam

jonas: ok — is this private with our control plane in their VPC (private control plane) or is it our hosted control plane talking out to them?

mika: private control plane + data plane inside their VPC. Customer said they only allowed 10.0.0.0/16 and S3 VPC endpoints. Their compliance team found egress to 52.94.123.18:443 and to a monitoring host in eu-west-1. They think keys might be leaving the VPC.

sam: likely NAT gateway or public EIP on a node. Can you share the security-group IDs and the VPC flow logs? Quick checks:
```
# check for NAT gw
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxxxxxx
# list SG egress rules
aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-aaaa sg-bbbb
# filter flow logs for dst ip
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /vpc/flowlogs --filter-pattern "52.94.123.18"
```

lara: customer DM pasted — they only have outbound rules: 0.0.0.0/0 on ephemeral ports for worker nodes (company policy). So that explains egress. Compliance wants a plan to restrict egress while preserving connectivity to our control plane and S3.

jonas: two parallel tracks: network isolation (inbound/outbound firewall rules) + crypto/audit (KMS/HSM, CloudTrail). For network: we recommend deny-all-egress + explicit allow for: (a) Redwood control-plane FQNs/IP ranges over HTTPS, (b) S3 VPC endpoints, (c) internal monitoring endpoints (if they host) or our accepted monitoring endpoints. Do we have an explicit control-plane IP set for them to whitelist?

mika: provided them this morning: control-plane endpoints are api.redwood-inference.com (443) and a small IP set: 52.94.123.16/29 (apex list for our control-plane in eu-west-1). I'll share the CIDR list.

natalie: for KMS/HSM audit — ask them for the KMS key ARN used for envelope encryption and CloudTrail time window. We need CloudTrail events for kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, and aws:CloudHSM events (if HSM). Suggested CLI: 
```
# CloudTrail lookup
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GenerateDataKey --start-time 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-11-06T23:59:59Z
# filter for specific key
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/cloudtrail --filter-pattern "arn:aws:kms:.*:key/0123abcd"
```

mika: customer says they use a Bring-Your-Own-KMS key: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/0123abcd. Compliance wants assurance that keys never left and to see KMS GenerateDataKey logs.

jonas: we can provide our request/response metadata: for private we do not export key material. We only call KMS in their account (GenerateDataKey/Encrypt) from within their VPC/egress path. We should fetch CloudTrail events and show timestamps and source IPs. If those source IPs are inside their VPC, that's good. If source IPs are external, that's a misconfig.

sam: temporary mitigation before full audit: lock egress on worker SG to only: 52.94.123.16/29:443, s3 endpoints (vpce-xxxxx), and any internal monitoring endpoints. Example terraform snippet: 
```
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_restrict" {
  type              = "egress"
  from_port         = 443
  to_port           = 443
  protocol          = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks       = ["52.94.123.16/29"]
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.workers.id
}
# then allow vpce
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_s3" {
  type              = "egress"
  from_port         = 443
  to_port           = 443
  protocol          = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.workers.id
  description       = "allow to S3 via vpce only (enforced by route table)"
}
```

lara: I'll propose that to them — they prefer deny-by-default. They asked if we can sign an artifact that proves key material never left Redwood.

jonas: we can provide an operational statement: for Private deployments our agents perform KMS calls from inside the customer's VPC (no external key transfer), and we don't persist plaintext keys. For HSM we can surface HSM audit logs if they provided HSM endpoint. But to be concrete we need the CloudTrail events and VPC flow logs from customer side.

mika: I've requested: (1) VPC Flow Logs for the window 2025-11-01..2025-11-06, (2) CloudTrail events for KMS key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/0123abcd, (3) list of SG IDs + route table entries. Ticket created: SEC-8422.

deploy-bot: Deployment to private-controlplane-prod scheduled at 2025-11-06T02:00:00Z — no changes to networking.

natalie: once they send CloudTrail, search for EventSource = kms.amazonaws.com and check SourceIPAddress. Example filter: 
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=kms.amazonaws.com --start-time 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-11-06T23:59:59Z
```

sam: if flow logs show NAT egress, remediation options: (A) remove NAT gateway and attach EIPs only to bastion (restrict nodes to priv subnets), (B) use AWS PrivateLink/VPC endpoints for all S3/Secrets Manager, (C) tighten SG egress. We'll draft a playbook snippet.

jonas: also confirm audit log retention policy — private tenants default to 365 days. For compliance we can offer extended retention (on contract) up to 7 years. I'll draft language and send to legal/compliance for an attestation letter.

mika: sounds good. Action items: @sam collect quick network triage (SGs, nat gw, flow logs) + propose terraform changes; @natalie & @jonas collect KMS/CloudTrail proof and compliance wording. I'll update SEC-8422 and reply to Acme. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:
